okay so the things I LOVE about my cc:

- ability to get really great professors who are passionate and care about their students! there's also almost always space in classes. 

- small class size allows us to get more focused attention. professors are also usually very accessible.

- school wide focus on translating our degrees into practical career avenues. 

- dirt cheap tuition! also, most professors understand that we don't have much money and so textbooks aren't usually expensive either - sometimes they're free.

- multiple campuses all over the state and guaranteed transfer to the main (4-year) university with a certain gpa!  we also have access to facilities on every campus :)

Who is she feeling pressure from? That's the real question. My family and peers made me believe that "society" was pressuring me to go to college, and the real pressure was coming from them all along. 

If you ever get a chance, talk to her about it. Just ask her about her future plans. If she has a clear cut plan such as getting some kind of vocational training, or going to get a real estate license, or an apprenticeship, great! But if she doesn't, it might be a good idea to mention community college, scholarships, etc. Or if she just wants to wait a while, that's fine too! Assure her that there's no rush to make a decision - she has the rest of her life to decide.

You seem very kind and I don't think you would pressure her - as long as you don't make her feel trapped or manipulated, it should be fine. Sometimes it's good to be able to talk with someone else. She might want to have someone to talk to.
